title: SAML assertion -> admin policy binding and auditable mapping checklist
creator: Priya Nair
description: Deliver a prescriptive, IdP-specific compatibility and implementation guide that ties incoming SAML assertions to RBAC v2 role bindings and admin controls, plus an auditable mapping trail. This ticket captures the design decisions, transformation rules, audit log schema, test matrix for Okta/Azure AD/Google Workspace/Ping, and an operational rollout checklist for enabling the feature behind a feature flag.
acceptance_criteria: A single documented mapping contract exists explaining how SAML attributes map to RBAC v2 constructs (roles, admin_flags, resource_scopes).
IdP-specific configuration snippets for Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, and Ping are present and validated against local test IdPs.
Audit log events include original assertion fingerprint, mapping decisions, policy-evaluation outcome and are stored with PII-masking and retention metadata.
Fallback behavior is defined when attributes are missing or oversized (e.g., group truncation, attribute precedence).
Automated test suite covers positive/negative cases for assertion parsing, mapping, and policy binding for each IdP.
Migration/rollback playbook exists for customers migrating from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 via SAML claims, with clear upgrade path and canary rollout steps.
tasks: Consolidate attribute names and example assertions for each IdP (Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace, Ping).
Define canonical internal attributes used by RBAC v2 (principal_id, principal_type, role_ids, admin_bit, scope_list).
Implement mapping/transformation layer with configurable precedence and attribute transforms (string->list, regex extraction).
Implement audit log emitter and schema for assertion mapping events and attach minimal assertion fingerprint (SHA256) not full PII.
Build unit and integration tests with SAML test IdPs and synthetic assertions.
Author admin docs and console UI hint text for SAML mapping configuration and troubleshooting.
Run canary enabled rollouts with telemetry to validate mapping coverage and error rates.
idp_compatibility_notes: Okta: Commonly sends 'groups' claim as array; recommend using pagination-aware group handling and a client-side group allowlist to avoid oversized assertions.
Okta: Provide recommended Expression Language mapping example to derive 'admin_bit' from group membership (e.g., user.isMemberOf('redwood-admins')).
Azure AD: Can emit 'roles' claim for AppRole assignments; treat 'roles' as highest precedence for role_ids, then fallback to 'groups'.
Azure AD: When using group overage, Azure emits a link to Graph API instead of full groups — include guidance to configure Graph calls or use group-filtered claims for production.
Google Workspace: Historically uses 'memberOf' or custom attributes; encourage explicit custom claim 'redwood_roles' to avoid ambiguous parsing.
Ping: NameID formats vary (transient, persistent, emailAddress); prefer using a stable 'eduPersonTargetedID' or 'subject' mapping for principal_id to reduce account churn.
All IdPs: Provide example SAML metadata snippets including <Attribute> mappings and recommended NameID format (persistent) for RBAC stability.
audit_log_requirements: Event type: 'saml.mapping' emitted on every successful mapping and 'saml.mapping.failure' on errors.
Minimum fields: timestamp, request_id, assertion_fingerprint (sha256), principal_id, idp_entity_id, mapping_rules_applied, resulting_roles, admin_flag, policy_evaluation_result, region, node_id.
Do not log raw PII (email, full NameID) — only include hashed or truncated identifiers per compliance guidance.
Retention: default 90 days for mapping events, configurable per enterprise tenant; support export to long-term audit sink (S3/GCS) with optional encryption via customer KMS.
Correlation: include trace_id and link to the request/response in the Console UI for easy incident triage.
Alerting: emit high-severity alert when mapping failure rate exceeds 0.5% during canary or 1% in production for more than 15 minutes.
test_matrix: Positive: Valid assertion with roles claim -> map to roles and admin false; verify access granted to expected scopes.
Positive: Assertion includes admin group -> map admin_bit true and ensure admin console flags are visible in UI.
Negative: Missing role/group attributes -> expect mapping failure event and deny by default (deny-with-warning).
Edge: Group overage from Azure -> validate Graph fetch flow or fallback deny and produce actionable log explaining missing groups.
Edge: NameID transient changes -> verify principal id stability when using persistent subject vs emailNameID and detect duplicate account creation risk.
Security: Assertion replay attempt -> mapping should reject assertions with duplicate assertion_id within replay window and log audit event.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Docs + feature gate behind 'saml_rbac_v2' flag in control plane; unit tests green.
Phase 1: Internal canary (10% of auth traffic) with verbose audit logging and high retention to debug mappings.
Phase 2: Invite-only external beta with 3 customers across Okta/Azure/Google; collect mapping coverage telemetry and fix IdP-specific edge cases.
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to GA with 24/7 on-call for first 72 hours, automatic rollback criteria defined (error spike >2% or auth latency >150ms p95).
Phase 4: Post-GA add UI helpers in Console for mapping preview, dry-run mode, and one-click export of mapping audit to customer.
